sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Server address setting
sections.what: Sets the web address of the Universal RAG server to the local computer on port 8000.
sections.why: Likely reason: a default for local use, so both parts can run on one machine.
sections.watch_out: If the value is changed without rebuilding, the page keeps using the old address.

summary: A template with one setting that tells the web page the address of the Universal RAG server.
purpose: Shows the owner which setting to change if the server is somewhere other than this computer.
why: Likely reason: keeping the server address in a setting means it can change without editing the page code.
how: The file holds one line: a setting name and its value, set to the local server on port 8000. Next.js is expected to read this value when it builds the page. The file does not say where it should be copied.
outputs: The server address the web page uses, once the file is copied to a place Next.js reads.
risks: The value is built into the page at build time, so changing it later needs a rebuild. The local address only works on the same computer.
debug: If the page cannot reach the server, check that this value matches the server address and port, then rebuild. Check whether a real settings file exists where Next.js reads it.
